newsitem.title: USA: Consolidated Papers Q3 hurt by price drop.
newsitem.headline: Consolidated Papers Q3 hurt by price drop.

text.p: Consolidated Papers Inc said Thursday that its earnings and sales for the third quarter were hurt by continued erosion of prices for coated and supercalendered papers.
Earlier, it reported earnings for the third quarter of $0.90 a share, down from $1.51 a year ago.

Consolidated added that demand for coated papers improved in the third quarter compared with the second quarter of this year as customer paper inventories returned to more traditional levels. It also cited typical seasonal increases in coated paper demand.
Shipments for the third quarter were 396,196 tones, down from a record 450,176 tons a year ago.

Consolidated Papers said its Wisconsin Rapids mill, which makes heavier-weight groundwood-free papes for books, brochures, corporate annual reports and catalogs, operated at 81 percent of capacity in the quarter. This was down from 100 percent of capacity in the third quarter of 1995, but up from 74 percent of available capacity in the 1996 second quarter.

The Biron, Wisconsin River and Niagara mills, which make lighter-weight coated papers for magazines, catalogs and newspaper inserts, operated at 88 percent of capacity in the third quarter. This compared with 100 percent in the 1995 third quarter and 81 percent in the second quarter of 1996.

Lake Superior Paper Industries, which makes supercalendered papers used in advertising supplements, magazines and catalogs, operated at 80 percent of available capacity in the third quarter. This compared with 100 percent in the third quarter of 1995 and 77 percent in the second quarter of 1996.

The Stevens Point Division, which makes lightweight coated specialty papers for consumer product packaging and labeling, operated at 100 percent of capcaity in the third quarter. This compared with 97 percent last year and 98 percent in the 1996 second quarter.
Superior Recycled Fiber Industries produced 19,626 bone-dry tons of recycled fiber from post-consumer office wastepaper in the third quarter, down from 24,202 tons during third quarter of 1995.
Shipments of corrugated products were up, as were shipments of paperboard products.
